subject: RE: Request for extended payment terms and credit ceiling
messages:
From: Emma Soto <emma@voltware.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Danny Lopez <danny.lopez@voltware.com>
Date: 2026-09-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request for extended payment terms and credit ceiling

Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week — VoltWare is excited about the latency improvements. Before we proceed to contracting, finance flagged two items we need cleared: a Net60 payment term to align with our vendor cycles and a temporary credit ceiling of USD 150,000 while we ramp usage across three product lines.

Can Redwood do Net60 for the first 90 days, then reassess? We can provide a PO but we prefer delayed payment cadence. Also please let us know what VAT evidence you need for our EU entities — we have cross-border invoicing that requires correct VAT treatment.

Happy to jump on a quick call if that helps.

Best,
Emma Soto
Finance Operations
VoltWare Inc.

Attachments: none

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Emma Soto <emma@voltware.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, rachel_kim <rachel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-11T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request for extended payment terms and credit ceiling

Emma — thanks for the clear ask and for flagging VAT. We can be flexible, but we have to balance runway risk across customers during ramp. Proposal below aims to get VoltWare the extended cadence you need while protecting Redwood:

1) Conditional escalator to Net60: Start with Net30 for invoices issued in month 1 and 2. If VoltWare achieves on-time payment (no late >7 days) for the first two invoices and usage threshold of USD 50k invoice/month is met by month 3, we will switch to Net45 for months 4–6. If on-time payments continue and cumulative spend reaches USD 450k by month 6, we will move to Net60 thereafter.

2) Credit ceiling: We can provision a temporary credit line of USD 150,000 subject to a refundable security deposit equal to 10% of the ceiling (USD 15,000) held in escrow for the first 90 days. Deposit returns once Net60 is granted or earlier if both parties agree.

3) Invoice waterfall and buffer: For months where usage spikes above projected caps, we reserve the right to invoice an interim milestone invoice (30% of overage) due Net7 to reduce exposure; normal usage billed Net30/Net45/Net60 per the escalator. This is a safeguard not an everyday process.

4) VAT/tax: To route VAT correctly we need VoltWare's EU VAT ID and a signed VAT self-certification for any non-US entities receiving invoices. Provide VAT IDs and an invoice remit map (country -> remit entity) and we'll ensure invoices include correct VAT treatment.

Attached: Redwood_SOW_v2.pdf (SOW with SLAs) and pricing_schedule_q3.xlsx (example invoice cadence).

If VoltWare is OK with the escrow and the conditional escalator, we can convert the SOW to a PO + DocuSign and have legal draft the short amendment to reflect the escalator and deposit terms. Vanessa and Lauren — flagged for finance + AM coordination. Rachel — can you confirm if this construct is acceptable from a legal/credit policy perspective or if we should push for a parent guarantee?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_SOW_v2.pdf, pricing_schedule_q3.xlsx

From: Emma Soto <emma@voltware.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Danny Lopez <danny.lopez@voltware.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request for extended payment terms and credit ceiling

Karthik — appreciate the pragmatic approach. A few clarifications from our side:

• The escrow deposit is acceptable if escrow account is managed by a neutral third party and fees are split.
• We can agree to the Net30 starter and the conditional escalator, but request that the interim milestone invoice for spikes be capped at 20% of invoice to reduce cashflow whipsaw.
• VAT: we will share the EU VAT IDs and a remit map by COB Friday; please confirm you will issue tax-compliant invoices once we provide these.

If Redwood can confirm the 20% cap on overage interim invoices and provide a standard escrow instruction document, I'll route to procurement and Danny will prepare a PO. We expect to sign within 3–5 business days once escrow instructions and the DocuSign are ready.

Best,
Emma Soto
Finance Operations — VoltWare Inc.

Subject: RE: Request for extended payment terms and credit ceiling — final terms

Emma — thanks, that all sounds reasonable. Summary of agreed commercial controls (this will be reflected in the amendment):

• Starter cadence: Net30 for first two invoices.
• Interim cap: Interim overage invoice capped at 20% of the monthly overage (we'll remove the 30% language) and only used when usage materially exceeds the forecast provided in the SOW. Interim invoices flagged as "OVR" and subject to standard dispute timelines.
• Escalator: Net45 granted after two on-time invoices + month 3 hitting >= USD 50k invoice. Net60 after cumulative spend >= USD 450k by month 6 and continued on-time payments.
• Credit ceiling: USD 150,000 with 10% refundable deposit (USD 15,000) held in escrow; Redwood provides standard escrow instructions and neutral third-party account. Escrow fees split 50/50.
• VAT: Redwood will issue tax-compliant invoices once VoltWare provides EU VAT IDs and the remit map; include VAT self-certification.

Next steps: Vanessa will send the amendment + DocuSign link (HubSpot:HS-47831). Emma/Danny provide PO and VAT remit map. Lauren will provision the temporary ceiling in our billing system once deposit clears. Rachel — legal ready to sign off on the amendment text? If yes I’ll send DocuSign today.

Thanks again — excited to get VoltWare onboarded.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_SOW_v2.pdf, pricing_schedule_q3.xlsx
